title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: FRANK'S SHOP
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Frank Mabry, a cabinetmaker in Louisville, Kentucky.
For forty years, Frank built the best kitchens in town. Alone.
He liked it that way. His shoulder did not.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SHOULDER
segments.quote: The greatest of faults, I should say, is to be conscious of none.
segments.author: Thomas Carlyle
lines: Then came his biggest order ever. A whole kitchen, due in eight weeks.
His wife Linda said, get some help. Frank said, I don't need help.
Linda quoted the Scottish writer Thomas Carlyle, like she does when she's winning:
The greatest of faults, I should say, is to be conscious of none.
Frank grumbled. Then he hung a help wanted sign.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE SLOW HAND
segments.quote: He that can have patience can have what he will.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: In walked Tasha Reed, twenty-three, a former barista who loved building things.
She measured every board four times.
On day three, Frank almost sent her home. Then he saw the Ben Franklin calendar on the wall:
He that can have patience can have what he will.
So Frank waited. By Friday, every cut she made was perfect.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: HANDS OFF
segments.quote: Leadership is the art of getting someone else to do something that you want done because he wants to do it.
segments.author: Dwight D. Eisenhower
lines: But Frank hovered. He grabbed tools right out of her hands.
His old Army buddy Ray told him what President Eisenhower once said:
Leadership is the art of getting someone else to do something that you want done because he wants to do it.
So Frank asked, what would you do? Tasha designed the drawers. They were better than his.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE COMPUTER
segments.quote: Learning is not attained by chance, it must be sought for with ardor and attended to with diligence.
segments.author: Abigail Adams
lines: Then the customer wanted drawings on a computer. Frank had never touched design software.
Now Tasha was the teacher, and Frank felt like a bear trying to type.
She wrote a line from Abigail Adams on the shop whiteboard:
Learning is not attained by chance, it must be sought for with ardor and attended to with diligence.
Frank practiced every night. His first drawing was saved as, Frank did this.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE NOTE
segments.quote: A teacher affects eternity; he can never tell where his influence stops.
segments.author: Henry Adams
lines: The kitchen was finished a week early.
Then Tasha said, someday I want my own shop. Frank's heart sank a little.
But on his bench was her thank you note, with a line from the historian Henry Adams:
A teacher affects eternity; he can never tell where his influence stops.
Frank read it twice. Then he started teaching her everything.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE NEW SIGN
segments.quote: Someone's sitting in the shade today because someone planted a tree a long time ago.
segments.author: Warren Buffett
lines: A year later, Frank works four days a week, and his shoulder is happy.
He planted a little oak by the shop door, thinking of a line from Warren Buffett:
Someone's sitting in the shade today because someone planted a tree a long time ago.
Then he repainted the sign. Mabry and Reed Woodworks.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Own your faults. Be patient. Lead, don't push. Keep learning. Teach. Plant trees.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Admit your faults. Be patient. Lead, don't push. Keep learning. Teach someone. And plant a tree for later.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And measure twice.
